subject: project:gdl
value: ELIGIBILITY PREDICATE for the WebFrank instruction_permutation path, and the cheap screen that decides a mixed schedule+recolor residual in one command. webfrank.apply_patch applies stages in a FIXED order - instruction_permutation first, then the register stage (copy_register_fields / recolors / register_fields) - and permute_instruction_atoms runs check_permutation_dependences on the PRE-RECOLOR image, i.e. on OUR register colouring. Therefore: a residual whose target schedule is legal ONLY under the TARGET's colouring is NOT WebFrank-eligible, no matter how obviously correct the combined transform is, because the intermediate permuted-but-not-recolored image is genuinely incorrect code and the guard rightly rejects it. Concretely, the rule is eligible iff the permutation preserves every def-use chain WHEN READ WITH OUR REGISTER NAMES. Two closures and two rejections on 2026-08-31 establish the split. ELIGIBLE (closed exact): camera_init_for_gamemode (two independent r7-based loads exchange), msgPost +0x30 (addi r25,r25,64 vs addi r28,r3,0 - disjoint reads and writes), msgDraw +0x1c8 (three li writes disjoint from an addi read-modify) and +0x3b8 (an FPR-defining and a GPR-defining load exchange). REJECTED: sysResetService and MBRenderText, both of which need the target's colouring to make the move legal - MBRenderText sinks stw r3,72(r1) past slwi r3,r0,2 where our allocator homed both the spilled value and the index chain in r3, and sysResetService moves addi r4,r3,@lo past li r3,0 for the same reason. SECOND, INDEPENDENT REJECTION GROUND, memory: _word_effects classes every non-r1-based D-form access as the single resource 'mem', so a load may never hoist over a store when both are R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 base-zero globals whose base the linker fills in. Do NOT 'fix' this by disambiguating on the relocation symbol - claim.law.gcb-sflags-relocation-alias.20260830.v1 proves this codebase has distinct symbol spellings (sFlags vs gControllerButtons+0x4) denoting ONE address, so different-symbol does not imply different-location and the refinement would be unsound. TWO ENABLING MECHANICS worth knowing. (a) MULTI-STAGE CHAINS: config units map to a LIST of patches and several entries may name the SAME function; they apply in order, so N disjoint permutation regions separated by branches or calls are expressible as an N-stage chain in which each intermediate image is hash-pinned (stage k's after_sha256 is stage k+1's before_sha256). msgDraw ships as two stages for exactly this reason, since permute_instruction_atoms rejects a region containing any control instruction. (b) A permutation stage and a recolor stage may share ONE patch entry when the permutation is legal in our colouring - msgPost and msgDraw stage 2 both do this. AUTHORING RECIPE that this lane proved out: derive every rule from the CURRENT raw compiler output (build/GUNE5D/src/<unit>/.postprocess/body/<file>.o when the unit is already a webfrank unit, else build/GUNE5D/src/<unit>.o) diffed word-by-word against build/GUNE5D/obj/<unit>.o - never from a park record's recorded offsets, which drift; then PROVE the finished patch list by re-running it through the real webfrank.apply_patch on a copy of the object and asserting the output equals the retail bytes, which exercises every guard exactly as ninja will. Never use the unproven_recolor_audit escape hatch to get past a bisimulation failure.
